verdict.rationale: ROS 2 is open-source and self-run, so data stays with the user. It records topic data to bags via `ros2 bag` and offers a Python API for reading and writing bags, so recorded data can be pulled out programmatically. Its message interfaces work as shared, structured data definitions, and the DDS middleware can be swapped at runtime, which reduces vendor lock-in. Missing for 10: any evidence that the bag storage format is an open, documented standard, a documented export or conversion path to common formats (e.g. CSV or Parquet), and independent hands-on confirmation of migrating data out.
